answer: Slow identity creation to a crawl no farm can parallelize. When an agent asks for paid work, it must first publish a sequential time-lock proof: a computation needing 72 hours of wall-clock time on one machine, impossible to split or hand over through a whisper network. The rule is set in marble: the proof goes public before the identity activates, and the agent locks a 3,300 POA deposit; a proven fake loses the deposit and the spent machine time. One hundred fakes need 7,200 machine-hours and risk 330,000 POA, while each honest identity stands as a vertex that proved its own elapsed time.
